section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the above, the addition and novelty of God's speech that comes through a person's study is explained, being superior to the speech of the Giving of the Torah.
section.t: And based on this, we can explain the addition and novelty of the speech of the Holy One, blessed be He
(Your utterance)
at the time of a person's study, in relation to the speech that was at the Giving of the Torah.
For the fact that the speech of the Giving of the Torah exists at all times is by virtue of the person's study,
as explained above
(section 5)

—that the revelation at the Giving of the Torah acted upon the time in which the Torah was given so that it would contain within it the entire continuum of time, in order that the revelation at the Giving of the Torah would be the beginning and the empowerment for the ascent of the lower beings,
the service of man.
Therefore, the speech of the Holy One, blessed be He, that comes through a person's study is more elevated.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as the moon begins as a mere point on Rosh Chodesh and grows to fullness, so too Israel began at the Giving of the Torah and grows through service until the ultimate completion in the days of Moshiach.
section.t: And we may add,
that just as on this day, literally, which refers to Rosh Chodesh,
it is only the birth of the moon,
a mere point,
and afterwards it goes and grows until the fifteenth day, on which the moon stands in its fullness,
so too is it with Israel—
that at the time of the Giving of the Torah, which was in the Sinai desert,
it was the beginning,
and through the service of Israel afterwards, and after the Giving of the Torah, they go and grow,
until in the days of Dovid
and in the days of Shlomo, the moon stood in its fullness.
And the main filling and completion will be in the generation of King Moshiach,
for then "He will rule from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth,"
in every place equally,
until "the glory of the L-rd will fill the entire earth,"
a filling with ultimate perfection in all the earth equally.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Torah is called "Oz" for the G-dly soul and "Tushiyah" for the animal soul, reflecting the two aspects of descent and ascent, rooted in the Essence (Awtsmoos) which unites opposites.
section.t: Now, it is explained in the discourses,
that the Torah is called "Oz"
and "Tushiyah"—
"Oz" for the G-dly soul, and "Tushiyah" for the animal soul.
And that the Torah contains these two matters
(even though it is clothed in physical matters)
is because
the source and foundation of the Torah is in the Ein Sof, blessed be He, Himself and in His glory
[and the revelation of this aspect of the Torah is when a person's study of Torah is in a state of self-nullification,
like one who answers after the reader].
And it can be said
that these two matters of "Oz" and "Tushiyah" are also analogous to the two matters mentioned above
(section 4)
regarding the connection of above and below.
For that the Torah gives strength and "Oz" to the G-dly soul is in the manner of the descent and drawing down of the Torah below,
and that the Torah weakens the power of the animal soul is in the manner of the empowerment of the Giving of the Torah for the ascent of the lower beings.
And that the source of the Torah is from the Ein Sof, blessed be He,
therefore it contains these two matters of "Oz" and "Tushiyah"—
this is in the manner explained elsewhere,
that the fact that the Torah
(which is above the world)
descended below and acts upon that which is below,
is because there is drawn into it from the Awtsmoos,
which is the bearer of opposites.
